name: Chicken Biryani
description: Pakistani chicken biryani layers fragrant basmati rice, spiced chicken, fried onions and herbs, then finishes on dum.
seo_description: Pakistani chicken biryani with basmati rice, spiced chicken, fried onions and low-heat dum, plus practical layering tips.
ingredients: 2 tbsp biryani masala, or to taste
½ cup chopped mint and coriander
method: Rinse the basmati until the water becomes much clearer, soak for about 30 minutes or as appropriate for your rice variety, then drain well.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and fry the sliced onions until evenly deep golden. Remove about half for layering, taking care not to let them become burnt or bitter.

Add the ginger-garlic paste and chicken to the remaining onion and cook until the chicken loses its raw exterior colour. Add the biryani masala, tomatoes, green chillies and salt and cook until the tomatoes soften.

Lower the heat and stir in the whisked yogurt gradually. Cook until the chicken is nearly tender and the masala is concentrated rather than watery; add the optional lemon juice after tasting the balance.
Meanwhile, boil plenty of well-salted water. Add the drained rice and cook only until partly cooked with a firm centre, then drain promptly so it can finish during dum.
Layer half the rice over the chicken, scatter over some mint, coriander and reserved fried onion, then add the remaining rice and garnishes without compressing the grains.

Cover tightly and cook over very low heat until the rice is fully tender and aromatic. Rest covered off the heat for about 10 minutes, then gently lift from the sides to combine without crushing the rice.
tips: Drain the rice as soon as it is mostly cooked but the centre is still slightly firm; it will finish steaming during dum.
Reduce the chicken masala until it clings to the chicken instead of leaving watery gravy at the bottom of the pot.
Taste the masala before layering and adjust salt then; seasoning is harder to distribute evenly once the rice is on top.
Spread the rice and masala in even layers so one section does not become wet while another stays dry.
Keep dum heat very low and use a flat tawa under a thin pot if the base tends to scorch.
Let the biryani rest briefly after dum, then lift portions gently from the side of the pot to keep the grains intact.

For the rice parboil, use a large pot of rapidly boiling water so the grains can move freely. Salt the water until it tastes pleasantly seasoned, drain as soon as the grain bends but still has a firm centre, and do not leave the drained rice sitting in hot water.
storage: Cool leftover biryani promptly, refrigerate covered and reheat only the portion needed until the chicken and rice are thoroughly hot.
serving: Serve hot with raita, salad and lemon wedges.
image_alt: Pakistani chicken biryani with long basmati rice, spiced chicken and fried onion
image_caption: Chicken biryani with long basmati rice and spiced chicken in a tighter food-first crop.
technique: The two stages that decide the texture are the rice parboil and the moisture level of the chicken masala. Drain the rice while the centre is still firm enough to finish on dum, and reduce the masala until it coats the chicken instead of leaving a pool of thin gravy.
doneness_cues: Fried onions should be evenly deep golden; very dark edges can make the biryani bitter.
Before layering, the chicken should be nearly tender and the masala should cling to it with no large pool of watery liquid.
Parboiled rice should bend but still have a firm centre when bitten; it finishes cooking during dum.
After dum and a short rest, the grains should be fully tender yet distinct rather than wet or clumped.
mistakes: Cooking the rice until completely tender before layering; the final steam can then turn it soft or mushy.
Layering over a watery masala, which sends excess steam into the rice.
Mixing or pressing the layers aggressively; long cooked basmati breaks easily.
Using strong direct heat for the full dum period; a thin pot may scorch before the top layer finishes.
substitutions: Bone-in chicken gives the masala more flavour; boneless thigh can be used but usually cooks faster, so reduce the masala without overcooking the meat.
If your biryani masala is very salty or hot, start with less than the listed amount and adjust after the tomato-yogurt base has cooked.
Lemon juice is optional; use it only if the finished masala needs extra acidity.
reheating: For a small portion, sprinkle over a teaspoon or two of water, cover and reheat gently until the rice and chicken are steaming hot throughout. Avoid repeatedly reheating the full batch.

faqs.question: How cooked should the rice be before layering?
faqs.answer: It should be partly cooked with a firm centre, not ready to eat. The exact minute count depends on the rice, so judge the grain rather than relying only on a timer.

faqs.question: Why does chicken biryani become mushy?
faqs.answer: The most common combination is over-parboiled rice plus excess liquid in the masala. Poor draining and an overly long or hot dum can make the problem worse.

faqs.question: Should biryani be mixed after dum?
faqs.answer: Rest it briefly first, then lift portions gently from the side so the masala and rice combine without crushing the grains.

faqs.question: How can I stop the top rice drying out during dum?
faqs.answer: Make sure the masala is not dry before layering, distribute the rice evenly, seal the lid well and keep the heat very low. If your pot has a thin base, place it on a tawa to soften direct heat; avoid repeatedly opening the lid because that releases steam.
